title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Must a fill be able to pass an untyped string constant as an enum field of a probe method?
description: ST-SUP-RC34-OC02-T01 expects the enum type ReservationRefusedReason to have Go constants, a fill that passes the untyped string "short" to fail to compile, and a fill that passes ReservationRefusedReason("lost") to compile. Go does not allow all three: a type with constants has a basic underlying type; when it is string, an untyped string constant is assignable to it, so "short" compiles; when it is an integer, the conversion from "lost" does not compile. Options: (a) keep a named string type with constants, as the generator emits now: "short" and ReservationRefusedReason("lost") both compile, and the runtime drops and counts "lost"; change the test to expect that "short" compiles and emits short. (b) a named integer type with iota constants: neither "short" nor ReservationRefusedReason("lost") compiles, and ReservationRefusedReason(9) compiles and is dropped; change the test to that. (c) a named type over []byte with package variables instead of constants: the test holds as written, but the values are variables that a fill can change. Recommendation: (a), because it keeps the declared text as the value and the runtime already drops a value that is not declared; (b) gives a stronger compile-time check if the owner prefers it. OC02-T01 stays not automated until this is decided.

title: How does the generated slot code make a loaded value from a validated request entity?
description: ST-SUP-RC34-OC08 says the generated code of a slot binding MUST make the loaded value of an entity from the validated request entity and give it to the fill, and the fill MUST NOT be able to make one itself. The loaded type is *loaded.Value[T] of the runtime package stego.dev/runtime/internal/loaded, whose constructor New only packages of the runtime module can call; the command and query handles make loaded values only from rows they read or wrote. Generated service code cannot call New, and an exported constructor would also be open to the fill, which shares the module. Options: (a) the runtime adds a slot binding constructor, such as command.LoadedFromRequest, that takes an unexported token that only a generated per-service package holds (for example a value that the slot component gets from the probe runtime at bind time), so the fill cannot call it with effect; (b) a slot binding's observations take no entity fields: checking refuses Entity.field in an observation that a slot binding emits, and OC08 is retired; (c) the slot component passes the fill the request as a loaded value made by a runtime function of the slot adapter, with the request bytes as the only input. Recommendation: (a), since it keeps OC08 and the rule of OC01 that only a runtime path makes a loaded value. OC08 stays not built until this is decided.
